brief: Goldman partner Mark Wilson argues this week's selloffs, French politics, Treasury auctions, AI financing chatter, OpenAI's revenue disclosure, and Samsung/TSMC earnings, were not negative news but 'tape bombs' misread by a market where US fundamental long/short hedge fund net exposure sits in the 1st percentile on a 1-year lookback, down from the 5th a week earlier, while Mag 7 exposure is near 22% of total US exposure, the highest since 2022. He frames the bond selloff as mostly a real-rate story, 98 of 108bps, driven by AI compute financing (SpaceX's $40BN, Broadcom's $50BN-plus) crowding out sovereign debt, a dynamic Goldman's Rich Privorotsky calls potentially immense and ties to why real yields are not falling. Wilson contrasts cheap Europe (13x earnings, 22% consensus 2H26 EPS growth, M&A at pre-GFC levels) against a US market where Micron and Nvidia alone drive half of the top 10's 68% contribution to Q3 EPS growth. His conclusion: don't fight the narrowness, since washed-out positioning should eventually force funds back into those two names, letting equities rally into year-end if energy prices stabilize. Nomura, Morgan Stanley, and BofA strategists are less convinced, citing bad breadth, a growth-scare risk from rates and energy, and record money-market inflows.
